overview: This 587-page file traces U.S. monitoring of Japanese fishing near Alaska and efforts to protect Bristol Bay salmon from offshore fleets. Coast Guard patrols, embassy reports, and interdepartmental correspondence document crab canneries, research vessels, treaty proposals, and Japan’s refusal to negotiate restrictions. Related records cover whaling, fur seals, fisheries disputes, and Japanese fishing across the Pacific and Asia through 1937.
interest: Patrol reports and diplomatic conversations reveal how uncertain evidence, conservation concerns, and licensing assurances shaped failed treaty efforts.
